$comment: The warnings and notices the e-invoice gate accepts (0027): each by the tool that gives it, the message as the gate keys it (`<severity> <type> <rule id>` for Mustang, `<level> <step> <code>` for KoSIT), the files of the corpus it is accepted in, and the reason it is accepted rather than fixed. Any other warning or notice refuses the file that raised it, as an error does, and an error is never accepted. An entry none of its files raised in a run fails the gate too, so an entry never outlives its reason. Read by scripts/e-invoice.mjs; held by scripts/e-invoice/registers.test.mjs and the judges' tests.

accepted.reason: Peppol's 'Document MUST not contain empty elements', which FeRD's EN 16931 schematron in Mustang 2.26.0 carries as a warning ('still status warning', its own words), and which KoSIT's EN 16931 scenario does not run. The Factur-X EN 16931 XSD requires one ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeDelivery and makes each of its four elements optional (Mustang 2.26.0's schema/ZF_250/EN16931, read on 17 October 2026). The reverse-charge sample gives an invoicing period (BG-14) and no actual delivery date (BT-72), so the element has nothing to hold, and the runtime writes it empty (packages/report-runtime/src/cii.ts), in the XML and so in the PDF that embeds it. A delivery date written to fill it would be a term the invoice does not state and the page does not print.
